en.title: Score Difference in an Optimal Number-Picking Game
en.description:
Two players take turns picking any positive integer from the remaining array, adding it to their own score and removing it. Player 1 moves first, and play continues until the array is empty. Both players want to maximize their own final score; find the absolute difference between the two scores under optimal play.

The standard input format, examples, and test data were written by CSWork.
en.input: The first line contains n (1..100000), and the second line contains n values (1..10⁹).
en.output: Output a single integer, the answer required by the problem.
en.explanation: In example 1, 4, 3, 2, 1 are taken in order; player 1 gets 6 and player 2 gets 4, so the difference is 2.
hints: The sum of all values is fixed, so maximizing your own score is equivalent to minimizing the opponent's. Sort the values in descending order, let the two players take them alternately, and compute the alternating sum.
